newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls curbing foreign investment in brewing.
newsitem.headline: China mulls curbing foreign investment in brewing.

text.p: China's State Council, or cabinet, is mulling a proposal to curb foreign investment in the domestic beer industry, the Economic Times said on Thursday.

The China Light Industry Association has proposed the cabinet restrict the beer output of wholly foreign-owned and Sino-foreign joint ventures to 30 percent of total national output, the newspaper said, quoting association official Wang Lizheng. The figure is currently about 20 percent.
The association urged the cabinet to restrict the domestic output of foreign beer brands to 10 percent of total national output, the newspaper said. They currently hold about three percent.
Association officials could not immediately be reached to comment.
Many state-owned brewers have posted losses and need injections of foreign funds to stay afloat, but China fears a foreign invasion of its beer industry, industry analysts say.
In principle, China will not approve new wholly foreign-owned beer ventures in the near future, the newspaper said.
The approval of the association would be needed in future for new ventures in which foreign investors have a controlling stake or those that manufacture foreign beer brands, it said.
New wholly foreign-owned and Sino-foreign beer ventures that manufacture foreign brands would have to export 20 percent of their output, the newspaper said.

Currently, there are more than 700 brewers in China. Their combined output in 1996 was estimated at 17.5 million tonnes -- the second largest in the world after the United States -- compared with 15.46 million tonnes in 1995, it said.
There are more than 80 brewers with annual production capacity of more than 50,000 tonnes, most of which have some foreign funding, the newspaper said.
China would throw its weight behind 10 domestic brewers, including Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd, Zhujiang and Yanjing, it said.
Their combined output would be boosted to 40 percent of total national output by the year 2000 compared with the current 20 percent, the newspaper said.
The association also proposed giving preferential loans and conditions to domestic brewers, such as offsetting debts with tax payments, it said.
Brewers would be restructured by listing shares or issuing bonds, the newspaper said. It gave no further details.
